candidates.heuristic_context: Target problem types: heterogeneous cases processed in a uniform way, so simple cases carry the effort of complex ones. Applicable when cases with clearly different recorded characteristics all follow the same path.
candidates.additional_context: case:ApplicationType = 'New credit' splits the log into 28120 and 3389 cases that are routed differently at 1 gateway(s), reaching 1 activities: 'W_Handle leads'. The mined model has no access to the attribute, so each of those gateways uses one pooled probability for every case — strongest example, case:ApplicationType = 'New credit' reaches 'W_Handle leads' 12% of the time against 0% for the rest (z=21.8), while the model sends 17% of arrivals there regardless. The redesign attaches the condition at every one of those gateways, so the case type is routed consistently rather than at a coin flip. ⚠️ The condition is a HARD predicate, so it sends 100% of this type to 'W_Handle leads' and 0% of the rest, where the log shows 12% and 0% — 88 percentage points of standardisation beyond what the log already does, which is the intervention rather than a reproduction of it. ⚠️ This changes WHICH cases go where, not how long anything takes: no hours are assumed anywhere, and whether routing by type helps, hurts or does nothing is for the simulation to measure. ⚠️ Direction of the change: in the log a case that reaches 'W_Handle leads' still records 3.5 further events and 0.168 h of further work, against 15.1 events and 2.230 h for an average case. Part of the case still lies ahead of it, so the rule shifts work rather than plainly adding or removing it.
